mainTopic: אלישע's bears, גחזי and יהושע בן פרחיה's student, pushing away gently, and the משנה on עגלה ערופה and things that ceased
overview: This amud finishes the stories about אלישע and then begins a new משנה. First, רב and שמואל argue whether the bears that attacked the boys were one miracle or two. Then רבי חנינא links the 42 children to בלק's 42 offerings: בלק was rewarded with רות, but his wish to curse also had an effect. Next, the people of יריחו call their troubled city 'good' because of חן, the natural fondness people feel for their own place. A ברייתא then teaches that אלישע was punished for pushing גחזי away with both hands. That leads to the rule 'the left hand pushes away and the right hand draws close,' shown through the stories of גחזי and of יהושע בן פרחיה and his student. Both students refused to do תשובה, saying one who makes the many sin is not given the chance. The new משנה explains what happens to the עגלה ערופה if the killer is found, and how conflicting witnesses are handled. It ends with a list of things that ceased: עגלה ערופה, the bitter waters, the אשכולות, and practices ended by יוחנן כהן גדול. The גמרא explains some of these on the next amud.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue: one miracle or two?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree about the bears that came out of the forest. One calls it a נס. The other calls it a נס בתוך נס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל: One says it was a miracle, and one says it was a miracle within a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between רב and שמואל about how many miracles happened when the bears came out of the forest in the story of אלישע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree something miraculous happened. They disagree only about how much of the scene was miraculous. The next step will explain what each side means.

keyTerms.meaning: A miracle within a miracle (a double miracle)

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree:
One says: it was a miracle.
And one says: it was a miracle within a miracle.
phrases.notes: They're talking about the bears that came out of the forest and attacked the boys (מלכים ב 2:24).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, חַד אָמַר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether the bears-and-forest event was one miracle or two.

steps.title: Explaining each side: forest only, or neither forest nor bears
steps.stepSummary: The one who says נס holds that the forest already existed and only the bears were new. The one who says נס בתוך נס holds that both the forest and the bears were created.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'a miracle' holds that there was a forest but there were no bears. The one who says 'a miracle within a miracle' holds that there was neither a forest nor bears.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each side of the argument means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the single-miracle view, only the bears appeared miraculously, in a forest that was already there. According to the double-miracle view, the forest was also created on the spot, so there were two miracles.

phrases.english: The one who says it was a miracle:
there was a forest, but there were no bears.
The one who says it was a miracle within a miracle:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעַר הֲוָה וְלָא דּוּבִּים הֲווֹ.
phrases.english: there was neither a forest nor bears.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר נֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two positions stated in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Single miracle means only the bears were new. Double miracle means both the forest and the bears were new.

steps.title: Why would a forest be needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the double-miracle view: why not have just bears, without creating a forest?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let there be bears and no forest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the double-miracle view. Why would a forest be created if only the bears did anything?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Creating the forest seems like an extra, pointless miracle. Bears alone would have been enough to punish the boys.

phrases.english: But let there be bears and no forest!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיהְוֵי דּוּבִּים וְלָא לֶיהֱוֵי יַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the double-miracle view explained in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that both the forest and the bears were miraculous
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The forest has no job in the story, so a miracle to create it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Bears get scared without a forest
steps.stepSummary: The forest was needed because bears are frightened in open areas and would not attack there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they would be frightened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the forest was needed so the bears would feel safe enough to attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bears behave naturally only in their own surroundings. Out in the open they get scared. So the forest was part of making the attack happen, and it was not an extra miracle for no reason.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the double-miracle view, the forest was created so the bears would be in their natural setting and not be afraid to attack.

phrases.english: Because they would be frightened.
phrases.notes: He means bears out in the open, with no forest around them, would be too scared to attack.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְעִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical reason why the forest was needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forest seemed to serve no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forest was needed so the bears would not be frightened.

steps.title: בלק's 42 offerings caused 42 children to die
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא teaches that because of the 42 offerings that בלק brought, 42 children of Israel were torn apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: Because of the forty-two offerings that בלק מלך מואב brought, forty-two children were broken off from Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא connects the 42 boys killed by the bears in the story of אלישע to the 42 offerings that בלק brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלק brought these offerings while trying to have Israel cursed. רבי חנינא says the death of 42 children was the result of those offerings, one child for each offering.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says:
Because of the forty-two offerings
that Balak, king of Moav, brought,
forty-two children were broken off from Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 42 children's deaths came as a result of בלק's 42 offerings.

steps.title: But בלק was rewarded for those offerings with רות!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא. רב taught that בלק's 42 offerings earned him the reward of having רות, and through her שלמה, as his descendants. רבי יוסי בן חוני confirms that רות came from בלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always engage in תורה and מצוות even not for their own sake, because from doing it not for its own sake, he will come to do it for its own sake. For in reward for the forty-two offerings that בלק מלך מואב brought, he merited that רות came from him, and from her came שלמה, about whom it is written, 'A thousand burnt-offerings שלמה offered up.' And רבי יוסי בן חוני said: רות was the daughter of עגלון, the son of בלק!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how בלק's offerings could have caused a punishment for Israel, when רב teaches that those same offerings earned בלק a great reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב uses בלק as proof that even a מצוה done שלא לשמה is rewarded. בלק's offerings were rewarded with רות and her descendant שלמה, who brought a thousand offerings. If the offerings brought a good reward, it seems strange that they also caused 42 Jewish children to die.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake (with a selfish motive)
For its own sake (with a pure motive)
Eglon, king of Moav, son of Balak

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for the principle that a person should keep learning and doing מצוות even with imperfect motives, because מתוך שלא לשמה בא לשמה.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
A person should always engage in Torah and מצוות,
even if not for their own sake.
Because from doing it not for its own sake, one comes to do it for its own sake.
For in reward for the forty-two offerings
that Balak, king of Moav, brought,
he merited that Ruth came from him,
and from her came Shlomo,
about whom it is written: 'A thousand burnt-offerings Shlomo offered up.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 3:4

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei ben Choni said:
Ruth was the daughter of Eglon,
the son of Balak!
phrases.notes: This explains how רות counts as בלק's descendant: she was his granddaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חנינא's statement in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that בלק's offerings caused the deaths of 42 children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב shows that בלק's offerings brought him a positive reward, רות and שלמה. So it seems they should not also have caused harm to Israel.

steps.title: בלק's real wish was still to curse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בלק's intention was to curse Israel, so his offerings also brought about a curse, even though he was rewarded too.
steps.simpleTranslation: His desire, in any case, was for a curse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both can be true: בלק was rewarded, but since he wanted to curse Israel, a curse also came from his offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act of bringing offerings earned a reward. But בלק's goal was to harm Israel, and that wish also had an effect, which was the death of the 42 children. So רבי חנינא and רב do not contradict each other.
steps.whatToRemember: בלק's 42 offerings brought him a reward, רות and שלמה. But because his wish was to curse Israel, they also led to the death of 42 children.

phrases.english: His desire, in any case, was for a curse.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּאֲוָתוֹ מִיהָא לִקְלָלָה הֱוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that both effects come from the same act: the reward from the deed and the curse from his intention.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the offerings were rewarded, it seemed they could not also cause harm.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because בלק intended to curse, his offerings brought both a reward and a curse.

steps.title: How can a city with bad water be called good?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the men of the city telling אלישע that their city is good. It asks how that could be, when its water was bad and its land caused miscarriages.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the men of the city said to אלישע: Behold, please, the situation of the city is good, as my lord sees, etc.' But since the water is bad and the land causes miscarriages, what is good about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of אלישע and asks a question on a פסוק. How could the people call their city good if it had such serious problems?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says the water was bad and the land caused miscarriages. That seems to contradict calling the city 'good.' The גמרא wants to know what was good about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The situation (dwelling place) of the city

phrases.english: 'And the men of the city said to Elisha:
Behold, please, the situation of the city is good,
as my lord sees, etc.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:19. The 'etc.' covers the rest of the פסוק: 'but the water is bad and the land miscarries.'

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּמַיִם רָעִים וְאֶרֶץ מְשַׁכֶּלֶת,
phrases.english: But since the water is bad and the land causes miscarriages,
then what is good about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּמַיִם רָעִים וְאֶרֶץ מְשַׁכֶּלֶת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was 'good' about a city with bad water and land that caused miscarriages?

steps.title: People love their own place
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין answers that a place has חן, a natural charm, in the eyes of the people who live there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין says: The grace of a place is upon its inhabitants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנין answers the question. The city seemed good to its people simply because it was their home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing about the city itself was objectively good. The people saw it as good because people naturally feel fond of where they live, even when it has flaws.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin says:
The grace of a place is upon its inhabitants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The city was 'good' in the eyes of its residents because people naturally love their own place.

steps.title: Three kinds of natural charm
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן broadens the idea. There are three kinds of חן: a place to its residents, a wife to her husband, and a purchase to its buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: There are three graces: the grace of a place upon its inhabitants, the grace of a woman upon her husband, and the grace of a purchase upon its buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן builds on רבי חנין's idea and lists three situations where people naturally see something as good because it is theirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן turns רבי חנין's point into a general rule. A person sees his home, his wife, and something he bought in a positive light, even if they have faults.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three kinds of חן: a place to its residents, a wife to her husband, and a purchase to its buyer. This explains why the men of the city called their troubled city 'good.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, שְׁלֹשָׁה חִינּוֹת הֵן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: There are three graces:
the grace of a place upon its inhabitants,
the grace of a woman upon her husband,
and the grace of a purchase upon its buyer.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. Either way, the point is that a buyer is fond of what he bought.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, שְׁלֹשָׁה חִינּוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי חנין's answer in step 9 into a list of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three kinds of natural fondness: a place to its residents, a wife to her husband, and a purchase to its buyer.

steps.title: אלישע was sick three times
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that אלישע became sick three times: for sending bears against the children, for pushing גחזי away with both hands, and the sickness he died from.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: אלישע became sick three times. Once for sending bears against the children, once for pushing גחזי away with both hands, and once with the sickness he died from. The פסוק hints at this: "And אלישע was sick with his sickness from which he would die."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with אלישע and brings a ברייתא listing his three sicknesses. This sets up the lesson about pushing people away that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses a word for sickness twice (חָלָה and חׇלְיוֹ) and also mentions his death. The ברייתא reads this as three separate sicknesses. Two of them were punishments, which shows that even a great נביא was held responsible for being too harsh.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Rabbis taught": this opens a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Elisha became sick three times:
one, because he sent bears against the children;
and one, because he pushed Gehazi away with both hands;
and one was the sickness he died from,
as it says:
"And Elisha was sick with his sickness
from which he would die."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 13:14. The two sickness words point to two earlier sicknesses, and "he would die" points to the third.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָאִין חָלָה אֱלִישָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of אלישע. Its first item, the bears sent against the children, refers back to steps 1 and 5, and it opens the lesson about pushing people away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלישע was sick three times. Two of those sicknesses were punishments, one for the bears and one for pushing גחזי away with both hands.

steps.title: Push away with the left hand, draw close with the right
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when pushing someone away, you should always use the weaker left hand and draw them close with the stronger right hand, unlike אלישע and יהושע בן פרחיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: Always let the left hand push away and the right hand draw close. Do not be like אלישע, who pushed גחזי away with both hands, and not like יהושע בן פרחיה, who pushed away his student ישו הנוצרי with both hands.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא turns the גחזי story into a rule for how to treat people. Even when you push someone away, leave them a way back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The left hand is the weaker hand and the right is the stronger one. So pushing away should be soft, and drawing close should be strong. Pushing with "both hands" means rejecting someone completely, with no way back, and the ברייתא gives two examples where this went badly.

keyTerms.meaning: An early sage who pushed away one of his students

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic guide for teachers and parents: correction must always leave room for the person to come back.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Always let the left hand push away
and the right hand draw close,
not like Elisha, who pushed Gehazi away
with both his hands,
and not like Yehoshua ben Perachya,
who pushed away Yeshu the Notzri, one of his students,
with both his hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם תְּהֵא שְׂמֹאל דּוֹחָה וְיָמִין מְקָרֶבֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the second sickness from step 11, for pushing גחזי, and draws a general lesson from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Push away gently with the weak hand and draw close strongly with the strong hand. Never reject someone completely.

steps.title: What happened with אלישע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the story of אלישע pushing גחזי away actually was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story with אלישע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the details of the אלישע incident. This sets up the next step, which brings the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only mentioned that אלישע pushed גחזי away. The גמרא now wants to know which event in the פסוקים this refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for the details of a story)

phrases.english: What is the story with Elisha?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֱלִישָׁע מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background of the אלישע example given in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the event in which אלישע pushed גחזי away?

steps.title: The story of נעמן's gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוקים: נעמן gave גחזי silver, and אלישע scolded him with a list of eight things he supposedly took.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And נעמן said: Please, take two talents." And it is written: "And he said to him: Did my heart not go along when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is this a time to take money and clothing, olives, vineyards, sheep, cattle, servants and maidservants?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the פסוקים about גחזי taking נעמן's gift and אלישע's sharp words to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע had refused payment from נעמן, but גחזי ran after him and took silver and clothes. אלישע's rebuke lists eight things, which leads directly to the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Aramean general whom אלישע healed of צרעת

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And Naaman said: Please, take two talents,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 5:23. נעמן is speaking to גחזי.

phrases.english: and it is written:
"And he said to him: Did my heart not go along

phrases.aramaic: כַּאֲשֶׁר הָפַךְ אִישׁ מֵעַל מֶרְכַּבְתּוֹ לִקְרָאתֶךָ
phrases.english: when the man turned from his chariot to meet you?

phrases.aramaic: הַעֵת לָקַחַת אֶת הַכֶּסֶף וְלָקַחַת בְּגָדִים
phrases.english: Is this a time to take the money and to take clothing,
and olives, and vineyards, and sheep, and cattle,
and servants and maidservants?"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 5:26. Here אלישע is the one speaking to גחזי.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיֹּאמֶר נַעֲמָן הוֹאֵל קַח כִּכָּרָיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by quoting the פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The incident was גחזי taking נעמן's gift, for which אלישע rebuked him.

steps.title: He only took money and clothes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the פסוק: גחזי took only money and clothes, so why does אלישע list eight things?
steps.simpleTranslation: But did he really take all that? He only took money and clothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the פסוק. גחזי took two things, but אלישע speaks as if he took eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olives, vineyards, sheep, cattle and servants were never part of the gift. So the extra items in אלישע's rebuke need an explanation.

phrases.english: But did he really take all that?
It was only money and clothing that he took!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי שָׁקֵיל כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The eight-item list in אלישע's rebuke (מלכים ב 5:26).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גחזי took only money and clothing, so listing six more items seems inaccurate.

steps.title: The reward for the eight שרצים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that אלישע was learning about the eight שרצים at that time. He told גחזי that he had taken his reward for that learning here in this world, matching the eight items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: At that time אלישע was learning the topic of the eight שרצים. He said to him: Wicked one, the time has come for you to take the reward for the eight שרצים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question: the eight items in the פסוק stand for the eight שרצים אלישע was learning about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע was not saying גחזי physically took eight things. He meant that by grabbing payment, גחזי was cashing in his reward for learning the eight שרצים now, in this world. The number eight in the פסוק matches the topic of their learning.

keyTerms.meaning: The eight creeping creatures that make things טָמֵא (ויקרא 11)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
At that time Elisha was busy learning
the topic of the eight creeping creatures.
He said to him: Wicked one,
the time has come for you to take
the reward for the eight creeping creatures.
phrases.notes: Count the items in the פסוק: money, clothing, olives, vineyards, sheep, cattle, servants, maidservants. There are eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה הָיָה אֱלִישָׁע עוֹסֵק בִּשְׁמֹנָה שְׁרָצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק: the list is a hint, not a list of items actually taken.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The eight items seemed to describe what גחזי actually took.
steps.terutzMaskana: The eight items match the eight שרצים, and they mean גחזי took his reward for that learning in this world.

steps.title: גחזי and his sons became lepers
steps.stepSummary: אלישע curses גחזי that נעמן's צרעת will stick to him and his children. רבי יוחנן says the four lepers in a later פסוק were גחזי and his three sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And נעמן's צרעת shall stick to you and to your children forever." And "there were four men who were lepers." רבי יוחנן said: This is גחזי and his three sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story by showing the punishment. גחזי got צרעת, and רבי יוחנן finds him and his sons in a later פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curse said the צרעת would reach גחזי's children too. רבי יוחנן shows that this came true by reading the unnamed "four lepers" in a later פסוק as גחזי and his three sons. This is the harsh, both-hands rejection the ברייתא warned against.

keyTerms.meaning: A skin disease that was a punishment, often translated as leprosy

steps.whatToRemember: אלישע pushed גחזי away completely, and the ברייתא counts this as one of his sicknesses. The lesson is to push away gently with the left hand and always draw close with the right.

phrases.english: "And Naaman's leprosy shall stick
to you and to your children forever."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 5:27

phrases.english: "And there were four men who were lepers,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 7:3

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is Gehazi and his three sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצָרַעַת נַעֲמָן תִּדְבַּק בְּךָ וּבְזַרְעֲךָ לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the פסוקים of the גחזי story with his punishment, and adds רבי יוחנן's identification.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גחזי and his three sons were the four lepers mentioned in מלכים ב 7:3, fulfilling אלישע's curse.

steps.title: Why did אלישע go to דמשק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק saying אלישע came to דמשק and asks why he went there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And אלישע came to דמשק.' Why did he go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about אלישע traveling to דמשק and asks what the trip was for. This is setting up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say why אלישע made the trip. The גמרא wants to link this trip to the גחזי story it has just been telling.

phrases.english: "And Elisha came to Damascus."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 8:7

phrases.english: Why did he go?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה הָלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גחזי story by asking about another פסוק involving אלישע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of אלישע's trip to דמשק.

steps.title: אלישע went to bring גחזי back, but גחזי refused
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says אלישע went to get גחזי to do תשובה. גחזי refused, quoting a rule he had learned from אלישע himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: He went to bring גחזי back through תשובה, but גחזי did not come back. אלישע said to him: 'Repent!' גחזי answered: 'This is what I learned from you: whoever sins and also makes many people sin is not given the chance to do תשובה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question: אלישע traveled to try to get גחזי to repent. גחזי turned him down by quoting אלישע's own teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after pushing גחזי away, אלישע still went after him to help him do תשובה. גחזי's answer is painful: he says that someone who leads many others to sin is not helped to do תשובה. That claim raises the next question: how did גחזי make others sin?

keyTerms.meaning: Turn back from your ways; repent
I have received this as a tradition (from my teacher)
Caused the public (many people) to sin
He is not given the chance or help (to do תשובה)

steps.confusionAlert: גחזי is not saying תשובה is impossible. He is saying that Heaven does not give such a person the chance or help to do it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that one who makes the many sin is not helped to do תשובה, is a well-known principle that also appears in משנה אבות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
He went to bring Gechazi back in repentance,
but he did not return.
He said to him: Turn back from your ways.
He said to him: This is what I received from you:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁחָטָא וְהֶחְטִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים
phrases.english: anyone who sinned and caused the many to sin
is not given the chance to do repentance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁהָלַךְ לְהַחְזִירוֹ לְגֵחֲזִי בִּתְשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why אלישע went to דמשק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלישע went to bring גחזי to תשובה. גחזי refused, saying one who makes the many sin is not given the chance to repent.

steps.title: How did גחזי cause others to sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what גחזי did that made the public sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he do (that caused many people to sin)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what גחזי actually did to make others sin. This sets up three different answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גחזי described himself as one who 'made the many sin', but nothing so far shows that. The גמרא wants to know the specific act.

phrases.english: What did he do?
phrases.notes: He means: what did גחזי do that caused many people to sin?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי עֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on גחזי's claim that he made the many sin.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific act by which גחזי caused the public to sin.

steps.title: First opinion: a magnet made the calf float
steps.stepSummary: Some say גחזי used a magnet to lift ירבעם's calf into the air, so people thought it was a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: he hung a magnet on the calf of ירבעם and made it stand in the air between heaven and earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: גחזי used a magnet to make ירבעם's idol hover in the air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A floating idol looks like a miracle, so people would trust and worship it even more. That is how גחזי's act led many people to sin.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (introduces one opinion out of several)
'The sin of ירבעם': the golden calf he set up for worship

phrases.english: There are those who say:
He hung a magnet-stone on it,
on the sin of Yerovam,
and made it stand between heaven and earth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֶבֶן שׁוֹאֶבֶת תָּלָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to how גחזי made the many sin.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He made ירבעם's calf float using a magnet.

steps.title: Second opinion: the calf spoke words of the Ten Commandments
steps.stepSummary: Some say גחזי engraved God's Name on the calf's mouth, and it would say 'אנכי' and 'לא יהיה לך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: he engraved the Name (of God) on its mouth, and it would say 'I am' and 'You shall not have.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second answer: גחזי made ירבעם's idol speak by engraving God's Name on its mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idol that talks, and even quotes the first two of the עשרת הדברות, would convince people that it was holy. So they worshipped it even more.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
He engraved the Name on its mouth,
and it would say "I am"
and "You shall not have."
phrases.notes: These are the openings of the first two of the עשרת הדברות, שמות 20:2-3.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: שֵׁם חֲקַק לַהּ אַפּוּמַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He made the calf speak by engraving the Name on its mouth.

steps.title: Third opinion: גחזי pushed students away from אלישע
steps.stepSummary: Some say גחזי's sin was keeping the Sages from coming to learn before אלישע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: he pushed the Sages away from (coming) before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The third answer is different in kind: גחזי kept people away from learning תורה from אלישע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion does not involve idol worship at all. Blocking people from learning תורה counts as 'making the many sin', because it took תורה away from them.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
He pushed the Sages away from before him,
phrases.notes: 'Before him' means before אלישע. גחזי kept the students from reaching their teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַבָּנַן דְּחָה מִקַּמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different answer to how גחזי made the many sin.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He pushed the Sages away so they could not learn from אלישע.

steps.title: Proof: after גחזי left, the study hall became crowded
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says the students told אלישע their place was too crowded. This shows that before גחזי was sent away, it had not been crowded.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the sons of the prophets said to אלישע: Look, the place where we sit before you is too narrow for us.' This shows that until then it was not crowded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support the third opinion. Right after גחזי was gone, suddenly there was not enough room for all the students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by inference. If the place only became crowded now, then earlier someone must have been keeping students away, and that someone was גחזי.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions on how גחזי made the many sin: (1) a magnet made ירבעם's calf float; (2) God's Name made it speak; (3) he kept students away from אלישע, which a פסוק supports.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha:

phrases.aramaic: הִנֵּה נָא הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אֲנַחְנוּ יֹשְׁבִים
phrases.english: Behold, the place where we sit
there before you is too narrow for us,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 6:1

phrases.english: which implies that until now
it was not crowded.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיֹּאמְרוּ בְנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים אֶל אֱלִישָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third opinion with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that גחזי pushed the Sages away from אלישע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 6:1: the place became too crowded only after גחזי left, so he must have been keeping students away before.

steps.title: What was the story of יהושע בן פרחיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second example of pushing a student away, the story of יהושע בן פרחיה, and asks what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story of יהושע בן פרחיה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the second story it mentioned earlier and asks to hear it. This sets up the long story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the גמרא asked what happened with אלישע and גחזי, it now asks the same about יהושע בן פרחיה. He is the second example of a teacher who pushed a student away too strongly.

keyTerms.meaning: An early Sage, the teacher in the second story
What is it? (What is the story?)

phrases.english: Yehoshua ben Perachya — what is that story?

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָה מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the גחזי story and opens the second story, built the same way as the question in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The details of what happened with יהושע בן פרחיה.

steps.title: When ינאי המלך killed the Sages, יהושע בן פרחיה fled
steps.stepSummary: While ינאי המלך was killing the Sages, שמעון בן שטח was hidden by his sister, and יהושע בן פרחיה ran away to אלכסנדריא in Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: When King ינאי was killing the Sages, שמעון בן שטח was hidden by his sister. רבי יהושע בן פרחיה ran away to אלכסנדריא of Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins with the background. It was a dangerous time, and the Sages had to hide or run away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains how יהושע בן פרחיה came to be far from home in אלכסנדריא. The rest of the story builds on this.

keyTerms.meaning: King ינאי, a king who persecuted the Sages
A leading Sage of that generation

phrases.aramaic: כְּדַהֲוָה קָא קָטֵיל יַנַּאי מַלְכָּא לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: When King Yannai was killing the Sages,
Shimon ben Shatach — his sister hid him,
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets, 'hid him.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya went
and fled to Alexandria of Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדַהֲוָה קָא קָטֵיל יַנַּאי מַלְכָּא לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question about יהושע בן פרחיה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Background: he fled to אלכסנדריא during ינאי's killing of the Sages.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח's letter calls him home
steps.stepSummary: When peace came, שמעון בן שטח wrote a letter as if ירושלים were speaking to אלכסנדריא, saying 'my husband' was there while she sat lonely. יהושע בן פרחיה understood that it was safe to come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: When there was peace, שמעון בן שטח sent him: 'From me, ירושלים the holy city, to you, אלכסנדריא of Egypt: My sister! My husband lives inside you, and I sit lonely and empty!' He said: 'I learn from this that there is peace now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: שמעון בן שטח sends a coded letter, and יהושע בן פרחיה understands that the danger is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter speaks as if the two cities are sisters. ירושלים complains that her 'husband', the great Sage, is staying in אלכסנדריא. The message is that he belongs back in ירושלים, so יהושע בן פרחיה realizes it is now safe to return.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; this shows that

phrases.english: When there was peace,
Shimon ben Shatach sent to him:
From me, Jerusalem the holy city,
to you, Alexandria of Egypt:
My sister! My husband dwells within you,
phrases.notes: The city of ירושלים is 'speaking.' Her 'husband' is the great Sage who belongs with her.

phrases.english: and I sit desolate!
He said: Learn from this
that there is peace now.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה שְׁלָמָא, שְׁלַח לֵיהּ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the letter that calls יהושע בן פרחיה home.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמעון בן שטח's letter told יהושע בן פרחיה that peace had come and he could return.

steps.title: The praise at the inn and the harsh excommunication
steps.stepSummary: On the way home, יהושע בן פרחיה praised an inn. His student took the words as being about the hostess. The teacher excommunicated him and would not take him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came back, he stopped at an inn where he was treated with great honor. He sat and said, 'How beautiful is this אכסניא!' His student יֵשׁוּ הַנּוֹצְרִי said, 'Rebbe, her eyes are narrow.' He answered, 'Wicked one, is this what you busy yourself with?' He brought out four hundred shofars and put him in נידוי. Every day the student came back, and the teacher would not accept him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story of יהושע בן פרחיה. It shows how a misunderstanding led him to push his student away harshly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher meant the inn or the hospitality was beautiful, but the student understood him to be talking about the hostess's looks. The teacher saw this as improper thinking and reacted with a very severe נידוי. Refusing the student every day sets up the tragedy in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An inn, and also the one who runs it. The double meaning causes the misunderstanding.
He excommunicated him (put him in נידוי)
Shofars, blown as part of a public excommunication

phrases.english: When he came back, he arrived at a certain inn.
The host stood before him, honoring him nicely,
and they gave him great honor.
He sat and was praising it:
How beautiful is this inn!
phrases.notes: The word אכסניא can mean the inn or the woman who runs it. The student took it the second way.

phrases.english: Jesus the Nazarene said to him:
My teacher, her eyes are narrow.
He said to him: Wicked one,
is this what you are busy with?
He brought out four hundred shofars and excommunicated him.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹמָא אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ וְלָא קַבְּלֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Every day he came before him, and he would not accept him back.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא, אִקְּלַע לְהָהוּא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after יהושע בן פרחיה received the letter and set out for home.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened in the story of יהושע בן פרחיה pushing his student away?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After a misunderstanding at an inn, he excommunicated the student and refused to accept him back every day.

steps.title: A misunderstood hand signal leads the student to idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The teacher finally decided to accept the student and waved his hand to say 'wait.' The student thought he was being rejected again and turned to idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day, while the teacher was saying קריאת שמע, the student came before him. This time the teacher meant to accept him and signaled with his hand. The student thought he was being pushed away for good, so he went, set up a brick, and worshipped it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its sad turning point. A small misunderstanding finishes what the harsh rejection started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher could not speak because he was in the middle of קריאת שמע, so he only waved. After so many days of rejection, the student read the wave as one more 'no.' This shows how pushing someone away too hard can leave them ready to give up completely.

keyTerms.meaning: The recitation of שמע, which one should not interrupt by talking
He signaled to him with his hand

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָרֵי קְרִיַּת שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: One day he was reciting Shema,
and the student came before him.
He had in mind to accept him,
so he signaled to him with his hand to wait.
The student thought he was pushing him away,
so he went, stood up a brick, and worshipped it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָרֵי קְרִיַּת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the daily rejections to the day the teacher wanted to accept him.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The student misread the signal as rejection and turned to idol worship.

steps.title: The student refuses to repent
steps.stepSummary: The teacher begged the student to repent. The student answered with the teacher's own teaching: one who causes many to sin is not given the chance to repent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The teacher said, 'Come back!' The student answered, 'This is what I learned from you: anyone who sins and causes the public to sin is not given the chance to do תשובה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the teacher trying to undo the damage, but it is too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student uses the teacher's own Torah against him and claims he is now beyond return. The next step explains why he counted as one who caused many to sin.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received as a tradition
One who sins and causes the public to sin
He is not given the opportunity

phrases.english: He said to him: Come back from your ways!
He said to him: This is what I received from you:
anyone who sins and causes the public to sin
is not given the chance to repent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזוֹר בָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The teacher reacts to the idol worship, and the student answers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The student claims he is beyond תשובה because he caused many to sin.

steps.title: Why he counted as one who caused many to sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the student's claim by quoting a teaching that he practiced sorcery and led Israel astray.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: יֵשׁוּ הַנּוֹצְרִי practiced sorcery, incited and led people astray, and caused Israel to sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the rule about causing the public to sin applied to this student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 quoted a rule about one who causes many to sin. Here the גמרא brings a known teaching showing that he did exactly that, so the rule fits him.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (introduces a known teaching)
He incited and led people astray

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Jesus the Nazarene practiced sorcery and incited,
and led astray, and caused Israel to sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 30 that he was one who caused many to sin.
steps.raayaObject: That the student fits the category of החוטא ומחטיא את הרבים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A known teaching introduced with דאמר מר

steps.title: Push away with the left hand, bring close with the right
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that with the יצר, a child, and a woman, one should push away gently with the weaker hand and bring close with the stronger hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: with the יצר, a child, and a woman, let the left hand push away and the right hand bring close.
steps.whatsHappening: After the stories of pushing someone away too hard, the גמרא gives the lesson in one short rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The left hand is the weaker one, so pushing away should be gentle and limited. The right hand is the stronger one, so bringing close should be strong and warm. The stories of אלישע and יהושע בן פרחיה showed what goes wrong when this is reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The whole section teaches one idea: when you must push someone away, do it gently with the 'weak hand' and keep drawing them close with the 'strong hand'. Pushing too hard, as in the stories, can cause damage that cannot be undone.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
the evil inclination, a child, and a woman:
let the left hand push away and the right hand bring close.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the general lesson drawn from the stories of pushing students away.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Pushing away should be gentle and bringing close should be strong.

steps.title: Killer found before the calf's neck is broken
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if the killer is found before the עגלה ערופה is killed, the calf is not holy and goes back to the herd.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the killer is found before the calf's neck was broken, the calf goes out and grazes with the herd.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts a new משנה about the עגלה ערופה. The first case is when the killer is found before the ritual is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calf is only needed when the killer is unknown. If he is found in time, the reason for the ritual is gone, so the calf is treated as an ordinary animal and may rejoin the herd.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf's neck was broken (the עגלה ערופה ritual)
It grazes with the herd (it is an ordinary animal)

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the killer was found
before the calf's neck was broken,
it goes out and grazes in the herd.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִמְצָא הַהוֹרֵג עַד שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֶרְפָה הָעֶגְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the end of the אגדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the killer is found before the neck is broken, the calf is ordinary and returns to the herd.

steps.title: Killer found after the calf's neck is broken
steps.stepSummary: If the neck was already broken, the calf is buried in its place, because it already did its job of atoning for the uncertainty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the calf's neck was broken, it is buried in its place. It came from the start for a case of doubt, it atoned for that doubt, and its job is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second case, when the killer is found only after the calf has been killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calf was brought because no one knew who the killer was. At the moment of the ritual that doubt was real, so the calf truly atoned. Finding the killer later does not undo it, so the calf stays forbidden and is buried.

keyTerms.meaning: It is buried in its place
It came because of an uncertainty

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that finding the killer later makes the calf 'a mistake.' The calf really did its job when the case was unsolved, so it keeps its status and is buried.

phrases.english: From when the calf's neck was broken,
it is buried in its place,
because from the start it came for an uncertainty;
it atoned for its uncertainty and went its way.
phrases.notes: He means the calf finished its job, so finding the killer later does not change its status.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁנֶּעֶרְפָה הָעֶגְלָה תִּקָּבֵר בִּמְקוֹמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case of step 33, when the killer is found after the neck was broken.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the neck is broken, the calf is buried, since it already atoned for the doubt.

steps.title: The killer is still put to death
steps.stepSummary: Even after the calf was killed, if the killer is found later, he is executed. The ritual does not free him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the calf's neck was broken and afterward the killer was found, he is put to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by saying what happens to the killer himself in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calf atoned for the community's uncertainty, not for the killer. So once he is found, he still gets the punishment of a murderer.
steps.whyThisMatters: It makes clear that the עגלה ערופה atones for the community's doubt and is never a way out for the murderer.

phrases.aramaic: נֶעֶרְפָה הָעֶגְלָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִמְצָא הַהוֹרֵג
phrases.english: If the calf's neck was broken and afterward the killer was found,
he is put to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶעֶרְפָה הָעֶגְלָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִמְצָא הַהוֹרֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the law about the killer in the same case as step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A killer found after the ritual is still executed.

steps.title: One witness against one witness: the ritual is still done
steps.stepSummary: If one witness says he saw the killer and another says he did not, or two women argue the same way, they still break the calf's neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness says, 'I saw the killer,' and another witness says, 'You didn't see.' Or one woman says, 'I saw,' and another woman says, 'You didn't see.' In these cases they would break the neck of the calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case: what happens when the testimony about who the killer is gets contradicted. When it is one person against one person, the עגלה ערופה ritual still goes ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ritual is only cancelled when the killer is clearly known. Here one claim cancels out the other, so nobody has clearly identified the killer. The killing remains unsolved and the calf's neck is broken.

keyTerms.meaning: They break the neck (of the עגלה ערופה)

phrases.english: One witness says, "I saw the killer,"
and one witness says, "You did not see."
A woman says, "I saw,"
and a woman says, "You did not see"
they would break the neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״רָאִיתִי אֶת הַהוֹרֵג״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's discussion of finding the killer. Now the question is what counts as 'finding' him when the witnesses disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one witness is contradicted by one other person, the killer is not considered known, so the calf's neck is broken.

steps.title: When the numbers are uneven: two witnesses decide
steps.stepSummary: One witness against two: the ritual is done. Two witnesses against one: the ritual is not done.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness says, 'I saw,' and two say, 'You didn't see,' they break the neck. If two say, 'We saw,' and one says to them, 'You didn't see,' they do not break the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the witness cases by looking at uneven numbers. Whichever side has two witnesses wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two witnesses deny the one witness, his claim falls away, the killer is unknown, and the ritual goes ahead. When two witnesses say they saw the killer, a single person cannot cancel them. The killer counts as known, so there is no עגלה ערופה.
steps.whatToRemember: The עגלה ערופה is cancelled only when the killer is clearly known. A pair of witnesses is what makes him clearly known, and one person cannot overturn two.

phrases.english: One witness says, "I saw,"
and two say, "You did not see"
they would break the neck.
Two say, "We saw,"
and one says to them, "You did not see"
they would not break the neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״רָאִיתִי״, וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים ״לֹא רָאִיתָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the set of witness cases begun in step 36 by adding uneven-number cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses override one: with two against the one witness, the ritual is done; with two identifying the killer, it is not.

steps.title: The calf ritual stopped when murderers became common
steps.stepSummary: When murderers increased, עגלה ערופה stopped, starting from the time of אליעזר בן דינאי, who was renamed 'son of the murderer.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Once murderers became many, the עגלה ערופה stopped. When אליעזר בן דינאי came (he used to be called תחינה בן פרישה), people started calling him 'son of the murderer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new theme: a list of things that ended over the generations. The first item is the עגלה ערופה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ritual was built for a rare, mysterious killing. Once murder became common and murderers were openly known, those conditions no longer existed. אליעזר בן דינאי is given as the example of the time this happened.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the Torah's law of עגלה ערופה was cancelled as a category. It simply stopped being carried out because the situation it requires no longer came up.

phrases.english: From when the murderers became many
the calf whose neck is broken ceased.
From when Eliezer ben Dinai came,
and he used to be called Techina ben Perisha,
they went back and called him "son of the murderer."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁרַבּוּ הָרוֹצְחָנִין בָּטְלָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the details of the ritual to the history of when it stopped.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once murder became common, the עגלה ערופה was no longer performed.

steps.title: The bitter waters stopped when adulterers became common
steps.stepSummary: When adulterers increased, the מים המרים of a סוטה stopped. רבי יוחנן בן זכאי ended them, based on a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once adulterers became many, the bitter waters stopped. רבי יוחנן בן זכאי was the one who ended them, as the פסוק says: 'I will not punish your daughters when they stray, or your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, for they themselves…'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second item that ended, in the same pattern as the first. This time it is the bitter-water test for a סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says God will not punish the wives because the men themselves are sinning. So when the husbands were not clean, the waters would not work on the wives. For that reason רבי יוחנן בן זכאי stopped the practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The bitter waters given to a סוטה

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the end of the entire סוטה ritual (the topic of this מסכתא) to a real historical decision and to the moral state of the men.

phrases.english: From when the adulterers became many
the bitter waters stopped.
And Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai stopped them,
as it says: "I will not punish your daughters
phrases.notes: הושע 4:14

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִזְנֶינָה וְעַל כַּלּוֹתֵיכֶם כִּי תְנָאַפְנָה
phrases.english: when they stray, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery,
for they themselves, etc."
phrases.notes: "And so on" means the rest of the פסוק, which talks about the men's own sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁרַבּוּ הַמְנָאֲפִים פָּסְקוּ הַמַּיִם הַמָּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 38: the same 'once X became common' pattern, applied to סוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bitter waters were stopped by רבי יוחנן בן זכאי once adultery became common, based on הושע 4:14.

steps.title: The 'clusters' ended with two great sages
steps.stepSummary: When יוסי בן יועזר and יוסי בן יהודה died, the אשכולות came to an end, as the פסוק in מיכה says: 'there is no cluster to eat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When יוסי בן יועזר of צרידה and יוסי בן יהודה of ירושלים died, the 'clusters' ended, as it says: 'There is no cluster to eat, no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another loss to its list. This one is a kind of person rather than a ritual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'clusters' are compared to grapes, something precious that the soul longs for. The גמרא will later explain exactly who counts as an אשכול. For now the point is that these two sages were the last of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The clusters (a special title for great sages)

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁמֵּת יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: From when Yosei ben Yoezer of Tzereida died
and Yosei ben Yehuda of Jerusalem,
the clusters ceased,
phrases.notes: This is a title for a certain kind of great sage. The גמרא will explain it later.

phrases.english: as it says: "There is no cluster to eat;
phrases.notes: מיכה 7:1

phrases.english: nor first-ripe fig that my soul desires."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁמֵּת יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of things that ended. It moves from rituals to a type of leader.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the deaths of יוסי בן יועזר and יוסי בן יהודה, the era of the אשכולות ended.

steps.title: יוחנן כהן גדול abolished three practices
steps.stepSummary: יוחנן כהן גדול removed the declaration of tithes and also stopped the 'awakeners' and the 'strikers.'
steps.simpleTranslation: יוחנן כהן גדול took away the declaration of the tithe. He also stopped the awakeners and the strikers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes this section with practices that one kohen gadol, יוחנן, did away with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first is וידוי מעשר, the declaration that one has given his tithes properly. The other two, the 'awakeners' and 'strikers,' were practices in the בית המקדש that the גמרא will explain later. This step only reports that he ended them.
steps.whatToRemember: This section of the משנה lists things that ended: עגלה ערופה, the bitter waters, the אשכולות, and three practices abolished by יוחנן כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Yochanan the High Priest
removed the declaration of the tithe.
He also cancelled
the awakeners and the strikers.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הֶעֱבִיר הוֹדָיַית הַמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more items to the משנה's list of things that ended, this time changes made by a specific person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוחנן כהן גדול abolished the tithe declaration, the awakeners, and the strikers.
